assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one transparent-background sprite master for a medieval isometric RTS game.
Input image 1 (gold.png) is the old gold deposit to REPLACE; input image 2 (stone.png) is a STYLE reference, not an asset to modify.
Redesign the gold deposit to have the same convincing, finely textured painted stone quality as image 2, replacing the crude flat polygons of image 1. One compact natural outcrop: a tall rugged split central boulder, two lower shoulder rocks and several small rock fragments around their feet. Natural layered grey-brown slate and pale quartz, with clearly readable rich metallic ochre-gold seams branching THROUGH the rock faces, some exposed chunky gold pockets and a few subtle golden chips close to the base. Gold occupies about 15-20 percent of the visible mineral face, no solid gold boulder. The veins must remain readable when the master is reduced to a 70 pixel wide game sprite. Hand-painted classic late-1990s detailed RTS sprite aesthetic, crisp shapes and material detail, no black comic outline, not shiny plastic or smooth low-poly geometry.
Composition: single isolated outcrop centered in a square image, full object visible with generous transparent padding. Orthographic isometric camera: ground axes at +26.565 and -26.565 degrees, 2:1 ground-plane perspective. Footprint is wider than it is deep, rough oval ground contact; rocks form a unified silhouette around 1.3 times as wide as tall. The rear ridge is higher, front fragments lower. Warm light from upper left; cooler shaded right planes. Only tiny grounding crevices, NO baked large drop shadow because the game casts dynamic shadows.
Transparent background with genuine alpha. No terrain tile, no square or diamond base, no grass carpet, no scenery, no miner, no tools, no building, no lettering, no border, no interface, no watermark. Output just one finished gold-deposit asset.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: depleted-state transparent game sprite paired with the supplied gold ore outcrop.
Reference/edit target: the supplied gold outcrop. Keep its hand-painted medieval RTS style, grey-brown mineral colors, top-left lighting, and orthographic 2:1 isometric ground perspective.
Show ONLY the exhausted flat base after miners have completely removed the valuable gold-bearing rock: a low natural bed of fractured grey and warm brown slate, dusty quartz shards, and a few tiny rough stones around the perimeter. Remove every tall boulder. Remove all visible gold veins and nuggets: this is an exhausted deposit, so it must not advertise resources remaining. The mound is very flat, roughly three times as wide as it is tall, with irregular rocky edges; a sparse arrangement of small chips reveals transparency between scattered perimeter fragments. No deep pit, no mined tunnel, no tools, no miners, no grass tile, no floor diamond.
One centered complete asset on genuinely transparent alpha background with padding. No cast drop shadow, no glow, no labels, no UI, no border. It will be packed at about 60 pixels wide in the game, so retain readable larger pieces rather than noisy specks.
